Here is an interesting fact about SpaceX that no one is talking about. Their satellites are in the low earth orbit. Well that comes with a cost. And that cost is that their orbits deteriorate and after about five years or so, these satellites fall into the atmosphere. And that obviously means they burn out and will have to be replaced. Think about that. SpaceX can never stop launching more and more satellites as long as the company operates. And if the StarLink business starts to plateau... what will that mean for the future of the company? I cannot see anyone talking about this, so hopefully Prof G could look into this and enlighten the investor community.

There's a number of commercial sats in low orbit. Putting little cube sats in low orbit was mostly a solved problem. Apparently they drift as well, their onboard propellant to adjust orbit runs out and it's cheaper to replace them than do a Hubble repair mission. They wobble apart for some reason.

This leads to another fun detail. The largest share of SpaceX launches are now Starlink ones. It's Musk buying from Musk again. It mostly lets them pass off as much launch costs as they want on SpaceX, while Starlink keeps the nice subscription revenue. There aren't many customers who want a massive increased launch capacity, but Starlink is an in-house customer.
